title: EPIDERMOLYSIS BULLOSA SIMPLEX 7, WITH NEPHROPATHY AND DEAFNESS

intro.text: A number sign (#) is used with this entry because of evidence that epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene (602243) on chromosome 11p15.5.

checks.claim: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is caused by homozygous mutation in the CD151 gene.
checks.evidence_quote: The 3 patients are homozygous for a single nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, causing a frameshift and premature stop signal at codon 140.
checks.explanation: Patients with nephritis, deafness and pretibial EB are homozygous for a CD151 mutation; the EBS7 name is the draft's own nomenclature.

checks.claim: The CD151 gene is located on chromosome 11p15.5.
checks.evidence_quote: It is encoded by a gene at the same position on chromosome 11p15.5 as the MER2 blood group gene.

paragraphs.text: Epidermolysis bullosa simplex-7 with nephropathy and deafness (EBS7) is characterized by hereditary nephritis that progresses to end-stage kidney disease, together with pretibial epidermolysis bullosa and sensorineural deafness. Affected individuals have been found to have the MER2-negative blood group.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) showed that CD151, a tetraspanin, expresses the MER2 blood group antigen and is present on erythrocytes. It was the first member of the tetraspanin superfamily to be detected on erythrocytes. They examined CD151 in 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease, 2 of whom were sibs. All 3 patients were homozygous for a single-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of CD151, which caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) stated that the frameshift mutation would produce a truncated CD151 protein without its integrin-binding domain. They concluded that CD151 is essential for the proper assembly of the glomerular and tubular basement membrane in the kidney and has functional significance in the skin. They also suggested that CD151 is probably a component of the inner ear and could play a role in erythropoiesis.

paragraphs.text: Karamatic Crew et al. (2004) studied 3 MER2-negative patients of Indian Jewish origin with end-stage kidney disease. Two of them were sibs, who also had hereditary nephritis, sensorineural deafness, pretibial epidermolysis bullosa, and beta-thalassemia minor. All 3 patients were homozygous for a single-nucleotide insertion (G383) in exon 5 of the CD151 gene. The insertion caused a frameshift and a premature stop signal at codon 140. The authors stated that the mutation would produce a truncated protein lacking the integrin-binding domain.
